To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) we formulate the problem of tweet level rumour classification as a supervised learning and domain adaptation problem, and (ii) we demonstrate that multi-task learning helps improve results.

1) we propose a supervised learning approach for the problem of tweet-level rumour classification; 2) our approach outperforms a state-of-the-art approach for this problem; 3) we propose an unsupervised domain adaption approach to tackle this problem, which outperforms the supervised learning approach when there is limited labelled data; and 4) we show how multi-task learning can be applied to this problem.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
multi-task learning with unsupervised domain adaption achieves good results on a new rumour dataset.
multi-task learning is an effective approach to the problem of tweet-level classification of rumour judgements, and it can be used for rumour detection and classification in social media.
multi-task learning is an important and powerful tool for the domain adaptation of social media data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

1) supervised and unsupverised domain adaptation are both useful in the task of classifying rumours; 2) multi-task learning is useful for the task of classifiying rumours; 3) the performance of our system is promising and comparable with state of the art results.

it is feasible to classify tweet level judgements on rumours using a supervised learning framework.
